newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse consolidates upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse consolidates upward trend.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week on Friday slightly higher to consolidate its upward trend compared with the previous week, stockbrokers said.
Active trading in blue chip stocks, including Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, was also behind the rise, they said.
The all-share index closed at 437.99 points compared with 436.30 points over the previous week.
"Overall the market consolidated its upward trend this week because most of the blue chips expect positive results including from BMCE and ONA Group," a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
BMCE, one of the market's largest capitalisations, rose three dirhams in one week to close at 405 dirhams.
Wafabank, one of the liquid stocks, also gained three dirhams over a week to close at 546 dirhams.
Speculation on the market predicts the bank will increase its capital as it planned to expand its branches throughout the country, brokers said.
Spanish-Moroccan Uniban bank gained five dirhams to close at 110 dirhams compared with the previous week.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, remained stable at 560 dirhams.

SNI stagnation coincided with the announcement of 1995 consolidated results for the first time. It posted $43.7 million consolidated net profits in 1995. It gave no comparative figures for the previous year.
Morocco largest private ONA Group was unchanged for the second week at 500 dirhams, traders said.
The group ceded its 86.25 percent in maize derivatives producer SOMADIM to British-Belgian group Amylum.
Traded volume on the official market was 25.9 million dirhams against 41.8 million last week.
